root_cause.text: In KVM x86 Hyper-V TLB flush handling, the slow hypercall path incorrectly used `is_guest_mode(vcpu)` to decide when to translate the input GPA, even though `translate_nested_gpa()` is only valid when nested EPT/NPT is actually enabled, causing invalid nested GPA translation to be attempted for L2 guests without nested paging.
root_cause.evidence: The patch changes `kvm_hv_flush_tlb()` in `arch/x86/kvm/hyperv.c` from `if (!hc->fast && is_guest_mode(vcpu))` to `if (!hc->fast && mmu_is_nested(vcpu))`, and the commit message explicitly says `is_guest_mode(vcpu) is incorrect` because `translate_nested_gpa()` is only valid if an L2 guest is running with nested EPT/NPT enabled.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix nested TLB flush handling to translate the hypercall input address only when nested MMU is enabled.
intent_record.what: In kvm_hv_flush_tlb(), the condition guarding nested GPA translation was changed from `!hc->fast && is_guest_mode(vcpu)` to `!hc->fast && mmu_is_nested(vcpu)`.
intent_record.how: This changes the code to translate the input guest physical address only when nested MMU mode is active, rather than whenever the vCPU is merely in guest mode. As a result, non-nested guests no longer take the nested translation path unnecessarily, while nested guests still get their GPA translated before the hypercall proceeds.

grouping_result.intent: Fix nested TLB flush handling to translate the hypercall input address only when nested MMU is enabled.

relevance_review.reason: The group directly matches the root cause: it fixes Hyper-V TLB flush handling so the input GPA is translated only when nested MMU/nested paging is enabled, addressing the invalid nested GPA translation for L2 guests without nested paging.

candidates.rationale: This condition triggers GPA translation based only on guest mode, not on whether nested MMU is enabled. As a result, the subsequent nested GPA translation is attempted for L2 guests even when nested paging is unavailable, which matches the root cause.

This is the incorrect operation performed under the bad condition: it attempts nested GPA translation unconditionally for guest mode, even though translate_nested_gpa() is only valid when nested EPT/NPT is enabled.

vuln_statements.explanation: This condition is the root cause trigger: it decides to enter nested GPA translation based only on guest mode, not on whether nested MMU/nested paging is enabled, which can wrongly drive the slow hypercall path into invalid translation for L2 guests.

This statement performs the invalid nested GPA translation that becomes reachable under the bad guest-mode-only condition, causing translate_nested_gpa() to be invoked even when nested EPT/NPT is not enabled.

commit aee738236dca0d0870789138ec494e15d6303566
Author: Vitaly Kuznetsov <vkuznets@redhat.com>
Date:   Tue Nov 1 15:53:51 2022 +0100

    KVM: x86: Prepare kvm_hv_flush_tlb() to handle L2's GPAs
    
    To handle L2 TLB flush requests, KVM needs to translate the specified
    L2 GPA to L1 GPA to read hypercall arguments from there.
    
    No functional change as KVM doesn't handle VMCALL/VMMCALL from L2 yet.
    
    Reviewed-by: Maxim Levitsky <mlevitsk@redhat.com>
    Reviewed-by: Sean Chri
bic_trace_step.reason: The snippet shows the new handling for slow Hyper-V flush hypercalls: "if (!hc->fast && is_guest_mode(vcpu)) { hc->ingpa = translate_nested_gpa(vcpu, hc->ingpa, 0, NULL); if (unlikely(hc->ingpa == INVALID_GPA)) return HV_STATUS_INVALID_HYPERCALL_INPUT; }". This is the exact kind of nested-GPA translation logic relevant to the root cause, and it already gates translation on the slow path plus guest mode and rejects INVALID_GPA. Therefore the vulnerable construct is not present in this commit version, and the fix is present here.
